content.thinking: I need to fix a word-frequency script with four bugs. First, the sort key `lambda kv: kv[1]` orders ascending, so it returns the least frequent words; also ties fall back on dict insertion order, which is brittle. The fix is `key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0])`, giving descending counts and alphabetical tie-breaks. Second, case and punctuation: "The", "the", "hat.", "HAT", "fell!" all count separately, so I lowercase each line and extract tokens with `re.compile(r"[^\W_]+")`, which pulls letters and digits and drops punctuation and underscores (hyphens split words, e.g. "well-known" into "well" and "known"). Third, `open(path)` has no context manager, leaking the file handle, and no encoding, so platform defaults (cp1252 on Windows) can raise decode errors; I use `with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh` and catch `OSError` in the entry point, printing an error and returning 1. Fourth, `sys.argv[1]` and `sys.argv[2]` crash with IndexError despite the `n=10` default; I read `argv = sys.argv[1:]`, default `n` to 10 when absent, validate the integer, and return 2 with a usage message when the path is missing. For the sample text the counts become the=4, cat=2, hat=2, and=1, fell=1, sat=1, so `top_words("sample.txt", 5)` returns the 4, cat 2, hat 2, and 1, fell 1. Tests live in `tests/test_wordfreq.py`, inserting `../src` onto `sys.path` and using `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`, covering ordering, case folding, punctuation, tie-breaks, the `n` limit, default `n`, empty file, and a missing file; run with `python3 -m unittest discover`.
